Vāmadevagītā
(‘Gītā [taught by the sage] वामदेव’)
------------------------------------------
This is one of the sixteen minor gītās found in the Mahābhārata. It occurs in the Śāntiparva (Chapters 92 to 94) and has 71 verses. It is in the form of a dialogue between the sage वामदेव and the king Vasumanas. This has been recounted by भीष्म to युधिष्ठिर. राजधर्म (or the duties of a king) is the chief topic covered here.
By describing the qualities of a good king and the characteristics of an evil one, the work places before us the picture of an ideal kingdom.
An ideal king follows the path of धर्म (righteousness) always. In this he has to be guided by a competent गुरु or spiritual preceptor. He has to assiduously cultivate great virtues such as self-control, soft but truthful speech, respect for the virtuous people, consideration for others and devotion to spiritual life. By relentless effort and diligence he should acquire competence in as many fields of administration as possible.
He should appoint the right man for the right place, take good care of trusted assistants and employees, and organise an efficient espionage system.
He should keep the following as top-secrets: strengthening defences like the forts; plans of wars; consultations with trusted ministers regarding the affairs of the State; proper plans for giving comforts and conveniences to the people at the right time.
In wars he should fight like a hero and treat the prisoners, especially the captured rulers, with kindness and sympathy.
As regards internal administration, he has to pay attention to the following factors: protect himself from internal enemies; take the help of reliable people who have proved their loyalty and efficiency; keep the taxes to the minimum level; be just and impartial towards the subjects; avoid haste in implementing the decisions and policies arrived at.
As against this, वामदेव also cautions Vasumanasa as to what a king ought not do by describing the follies of a bad king.
A bad king not only abandons धर्म but also wilfully follows अधर्म (evil ways). He rules by force, oppresses the weak but gives a free hand to the wicked. Leading an immoral life himself, he encourages it in others. He ignores the गुरु and the good ministers (if any), employs evil persons and knaves to assist him and harasses his subjects. Neglecting the time-tested traditions, being indifferent towards well-wishers and the welfare of the State he ultimately ruins himself and the kingdom.

Vāmanapurāṇa
------------------------------------------
This is a comparatively short purāṇa listed among the Mahāpurāṇas. It was probably compiled during the period A.

-900. The extant version has 5400 verses, spread over 95 adhyāyas or chapters, though, according to the Matsya and the Vāyu पुराणस्, it has 10,000 verses.
There seems to have been a second part of this purāṇa called Bṛhad-वामन-purāṇa which, however, is not available now.
It was narrated by the sage पुलस्त्य to नारद at his request.
As the name indicates, it is concerned with the अवतार of विष्णु as वामन, the fifth इन्चर्नतिओन् among the दशावतारस् and hence a Vaiṣṇava purāṇa. However, equal importance and reverence have been accorded to शिव and देवी also.
The story of वामन and बलि (the king of असुरस्) has been narrated in great detail in the following chapters; 73; 74; 75; 77; 89; 91; 92; 93; 94; 95.
Other subjects dealt with are: शिव cutting off one of the five heads of ब्रह्मा; शिव redeemed at वाराणसी; destruction of दक्ष’s sacrifice; सती (Śiva’s wife) immolating herself and reborn as पार्वती, the daughter of हिमालयस्; शिव burning up काम (the god Eros); observance of certain vratas like Kālāṣṭamī; story of दुर्गा, महिषासुर and Andhaka; greatness of the सरस्वती रिवेर्; detailed description of कुरुक्षेत्र and pilgrim centres associated with it; story of दण्डक and दण्ड-kāraṇya including शुक्राचार्य’s curse; various incidents connected with प्रह्लाद; and, story of Gajendra’s deliverance.
Several topics dealt with in the dharmaśāstra treatises have been described here, such as—tīrthas (holy rivers); सदाचार (good conduct); sāmanya-धर्म (virtues common for all); आश्रम-धर्म (duties of the four stages of life); vratas (religious observances); कर्म theory and its application.
Unlike other पुराणस्, this purāṇa does not give the genealogies of kings and sages. However, detailed geographical descriptions of mountains, rivers and janapadas (countries) are found here.
The mountains are: महेन्द्र, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimān, Ṛkṣa, विन्ध्य, and Pāriyātra.
The various rivers arising from there are also mentioned.
The janapadas divided according to the traditional directions are: अङ्ग, बाह्लीक, Bhārakaccha, चौल, काम्भोज, Kerala, Prāgjyotiṣa, पुण्ड्र, Surāṣṭra, Tuṣāra, and Vaṅga.
Some of the social customs that prevailed were: early मर्रिअगे; śulka-धर्म (bridegroom’s parents giving money and presents to the bride); restriction of freedom to girls and women; सती-custom prevalent in certain sections of the society; disfavour of पोल्य्गम्य् and having too many offsprings; killing of animals and felling of trees frowned upon; strict adherence to the caste-system but possibility of attaining the status of a ब्राह्मण by taking bath in certain holy rivers (observing all the necessary disciplines) accepted.
Though the language of the work is similar to that of the general पुराणस्, it often rises to great literary heights while describing the seasons, the mountains, city of वाराणसी and the battles between the देवस् and असुरस्.
See DAŚĀVATĀRAS and PURĀṆAS.

Vāmana
------------------------------------------
Vāmana is the fifth अवतार or इन्चर्नतिओन् of Lord विष्णु.
See AVATĀRA and DAŚĀVATĀRAS.
The concept of वामन as त्रिविक्रम is very ancient and is found in the वेदस् (vide Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa

; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 1.6.1), as also many पुराणस्.
Iconographical works describe him as a short-statured brahmacāri (Vedic student) with two arms holding a chatra (umbrella), दण्ड (staff) and कमण्डलु (water-pot). He wears a kaupīna (loin-cloth) and has a śikhā (tuft of hair) on his head.
Several varieties of Vāmana—such as दधि-वामन and Viśva-vāmana—are sometimes mentioned in some works of tantra.
Vāmana also figures in the list of 24 aspects of विष्णु (See CATURVIṀŚATI MŪRTI.).

Vāmadeva
------------------------------------------
Vāmadeva is a sage well-known in the उपनिषद्स्. The Aitareya Upaniṣad (
) says he had realised the आत्मन् even while in the womb of his मोथेर्. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (

) declares that the sage वामदेव realised ब्रह्मन् and hence his identity with मनु and सूर्य. The Rāma-pūrva-tāpanī Upaniṣad (6.16) describes that राम was worshipped by great sages like वसिष्ठ and वामदेव.
According to the Śivapurāṇa (Kailāsakhaṇḍa 11.12) he learnt about प्रणव from Kumārasvāmi (Ṣaṇmukha or सुब्रह्मण्य) and taught it to other sages.
Ātreya was his disciple.
Vāmadeva is also one of the five aspects of शिव (See PAÑCĀNANA.)
